question.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{3}t,\,{t}^{2},\,t+1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
question.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,2t,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\sqrt{3},\,2t,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\sqrt{3})}^{2}+{(2t)}^{2}+{(1)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{4t}{2\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{1+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
